channel.title: Tech-Economic Times
channel.description: Get the latest technology news, AI developments, startup funding updates, business enterprise and IT industry insights, cybersecurity alerts, and digital policy trends from India and around the world on ET Tech

item.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says he would cut off customers who build unsafe AI
item.description: Nvidia is the dominant supplier of artificial intelligence accelerators, the chips used to train and run AI models. That’s put it at the center of a debate over whether the software risks growing too powerful and slipping out of human control. AI executives such as Anthropic PBC CEO Dario Amodei have proposed an industrywide slowdown to address the concerns.

item.title: Eight US states sue OpenAI, claiming ChatGPT harms children
item.description: The lawsuits, which were filed in state courts, are seeking an order forcing OpenAI to make changes to how ChatGPT works for children. The states are also seeking an order forcing the company to give up profits it has generated from young users.

item.title: Healthtech startup Confido Health raises $12.5 million in funding led by Z47
item.description: Founded in 2022 by Chetan Reddy and Vichar Shroff, Confido Health develops artificial intelligence (AI) agents that automate administrative tasks for healthcare providers, including patient calls, appointment scheduling, insurance verification, prescription refills and payment follow-ups.

item.title: Mexico to require digital platforms to protect minors from violent, sexual content
item.description: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum said on Wednesday that she would sign a presidential decree later in the day requiring digital platforms, including social networks and streaming sites, to shield children and teenagers from violent, sexual and other harmful content

item.title: Udaan sees growth after four years with 13% rise in revenues
item.description: Udaan has shifted to a cluster-led operating model with greater accountability for performance at the city and category levels, according to Vishnu Menon, the company’s senior vice president, business finance. The approach marks a move away from expanding across markets towards improving efficiency and profitability in existing ones, he said.

item.title: EU Commission is in dialogue with Google: spokesperson
item.description: The European Commission said on Wednesday it was "in dialogue with Google" over actions the company may take in response to the $1 billion fines imposed by the EU in July and required changes to its app store and its search engine.

item.title: Netflix cuts about 6% of jobs: WSJ
item.description: This marks its biggest round of layoffs since 2022, as the streaming giant faces intense competition for users' time in a consolidated media market.

item.title: Anthropic opens office in Singapore, partners with government on AI safety and adoption
item.description: The new office is Anthropic's fifth in the Asia-Pacific region. The company said Singapore is one of its most active markets globally, with its Claude AI assistant being used by businesses and government services serving millions of people every day.

item.title: Japan to invest up to $21 billion in two US chip factories to be run by GlobalFoundries
item.description: The move is part of a deal for Japan to invest $550 billion in the US struck by President Donald Trump's administration last year in return for the US lowering tariffs on Japanese cars and other imports from at least 25% to 15%.

item.title: Is your business easy to find and remember online? How can Indian founders choose the right domain?
item.description: While many Indian entrepreneurs prioritize social media for marketing, they often overlook the significance of establishing a robust website presence. A well-chosen domain name is essential for elevating brand visibility and forming a strong connection with consumers. This choice not only symbolizes the business's identity and its advancement goals but also underscores the importance of maintaining domain security and accessibility to facilitate seamless communication.

item.title: Navratri 2026: Top laptop deals across leading brands and budgets
item.description: Celebrate Navratri 2026 by enhancing your tech with new laptops! This festive season, leading brands like HP and Lenovo offer exciting deals, along with Bajaj Finance's flexible EMI loans making it easier to manage costs. Buyers are encouraged to find zero down payment options and compare model features. It’s essential to check the repayment details and eligibility criteria at Bajaj Finance partner outlets for a smooth purchasing experience.

item.title: Italy data centre connection requests top 100 GW, Terna CEO says
item.description: Italy's grid operator Terna has received connection requests for nearly 600 data centre projects totalling more than 100 gigawatts (GW), CEO Pasqualino Monti said at an event.

item.title: Space startups secure record $20.8 billion funding as infrastructure bets surge, report shows
item.description: Space startups attracted a record $20.8 billion in funding in the third quarter, as investors poured money into launch providers, manufacturing and other infrastructure ventures, according to a report by global investment firm Seraphim.

item.title: LSEG taps Nvidia for faster historical market data processing
item.description: LSEG, which operates the London Stock Exchange and provides data and analytics, has been expanding its offerings to support diverse demand whilst retaining licenses and control as AI also affects how businesses trade and consume data.

item.title: Singapore data centre developer DayOne's billings surpass 1 gigawatt
item.description: Singapore-based data centre developer DayOne said on Wednesday its total billings exceeded 1 gigawatt (GW), a day after financing for its expansion in Malaysia was increased to $7.2 billion.

item.title: Apple vs OpenAI: What the trade secret theft lawsuit is about
item.description: In the lawsuit, which was filed in July, Apple accused OpenAI, io Products and two former employees, Chang Liu and Yu-Ting “Alyssa” Peng, of taking or using its trade secrets and breaking confidentiality agreements.

item.title: South Korea finds hacking incidents at total of 16 financial firms
item.description: South Korea has found hacking incidents at a total of 16 financial firms and around 100,000 cases of data leaks so far, the country's financial regulator said on Wednesday.

item.title: Why AI makes computer worms harder to stop
item.description: Anthropic's warning that AI-powered "worms" could soon spread across smart gadgets is the latest in a series of studies showing how artificial intelligence could supercharge self-spreading malware. A computer worm is malicious software that spreads between devices on its own.

item.title: US lauds tech giants' role in cracking West African scam centers
item.description: The US Justice Department on Tuesday praised Meta and other tech giants for their support in dismantling online scams in West Africa. The Justice Department provided more details on Tuesday, saying it was coordinated with the UK's National Crime Agency and describing it as the first of its kind in West Africa.

item.title: EU takes a page from Ireland's AI playbook
item.description: The EU wants to catch up in the AI race by taking a cue from Ireland -- an early adopter of the technology which has rolled out the red carpet for data centres despite local backlash. The EU wants to ramp up its capacity and is pouring billions into so-called AI gigafactories made up of advanced AI processors and energy-efficient data centres for companies and research labs.

item.title: GameStop CEO Ryan Cohen buys shares worth nearly $23 million
item.description: GameStop CEO Ryan Cohen bought about $22.8 million worth of the videogame retailer's shares, a regulatory filing showed on Tuesday, raising his total ownership to 9.1%.

item.title: SoftBank junk bond sale raises stakes for CEO Son's all-in AI bet
item.description: SoftBank's promise to pay its highest-ever yields in a record $11 billion junk-bond offering highlights the pressure on CEO Masayoshi Son to secure returns on his all-in bet on AI amid concerns about possible overheating in the market.

item.title: Anthropic seeks rehearing of case over Pentagon's security risk branding
item.description: Anthropic asked a US appeals court on Tuesday to reconsider a ruling that upheld the Pentagon's decision to label the AI company as a national security supply chain risk over a dispute about safety guardrails on its technology.

item.title: UPI MDR rollout pushed; India’s first quantum computer coming soon
item.description: Happy Wednesday! The implementation of MDR on select UPI payments has been deferred beyond Diwali. This and more in today’s ETtech Morning Dispatch.

item.title: Nvidia buys stakes in four French tech startups: Report
item.description: Doctolib had said previously that Nvidia had agreed to buy a minority stake without specifying the size of the stake or its value, though it said the presence of Nvidia would help it to develop artificial intelligence tools.

item.title: Delaware jury awards Qualcomm $2 in damages, finds Arm breached license agreement
item.description: A Delaware jury awarded Qualcomm $2 in nominal damages after finding Arm Holdings breached its architectural license agreement and intentionally sought to disrupt Qualcomm's business, a Qualcomm spokesperson said on Tuesday.

item.title: Google launches flagship AI model Gemini 4 Argon for developers, businesses
item.description: Alphabet's Google on Wednesday released its flagship AI model Gemini 4 Argon to developers and businesses worldwide, seeking to regain ground against rivals OpenAI and Anthropic after months of delays and a leadership shakeup at its DeepMind lab.

item.title: In a first, AI helps UK lawmaker find her voice in parliament
item.description: A British lawmaker made history on Tuesday by becoming the first person to use an AI-generated voice to deliver a speech in the UK parliament. During a debate about health on Tuesday, AI software was used to recreate the sound of her voice, as it used to be, to read a speech she wrote herself.

item.title: EU watchdog says smart glasses must give 'clear warnings' when recording
item.description: The European Union's central data regulator on Tuesday said smart glasses should give "clear warnings" when they are recording, after a public outcry in recent months over secretly filmed footage of girls and women. The European Data Protection Board (EDPB) warned in its non-binding guidance to users and manufacturers that smart glasses raised "serious privacy concerns" as it seeks to increase awareness about the risks.

item.title: Govt seeks expedited development of AI tool to detect child sexual abuse material online
item.description: The issue came up for discussion during Union Minister for Women and Child Development Annpurna Devi's visit to the office of the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) here.

item.title: Anthropic warns of AI 'worms' spreading across smart gadgets
item.description: Small artificial intelligence models may be only months away from being able to behave like a computer worm, copying themselves from one internet-connected gadget to the next without human help, AI giant Anthropic said. An AI worm of this kind would likely be slow, taking days to copy itself, William Zhou and Daniel Freeman of Anthropic said, comparing it to a slime mold or a swarm of fruit flies.

item.title: AI services may account for almost half of Infosys' work in 2-3 years: CEO Salil Parekh
item.description: Parekh said the business, which includes building AI agents, coding work and modernising old technology for clients, is small relative to the company's size but growing so fast that it could account for 20-30% of Infosys' work within a few quarters if the current pace continues.

item.title: High data centre, chip costs and cheaper AI models pose risks to capacity usage: Infosys CEO
item.description: High data centre and chip costs, coupled with emerging AI models offering cheaper inference, pose risks to AI infrastructure investments and future capacity utilisation, Infosys CEO Salil Parekh said.

item.title: Bumble swipes right on $1.3 billion go-private deal amid online dating industry reset
item.description: Bumble said on Tuesday it had agreed to be taken private by Ithaca Holdings in a deal valued at $1.3 billion, as the dating app pushes forward with its months-long turnaround amid

item.title: Urban Company eyes Rs 2,500 crore QIP amid cash-intensive househelp battle
item.description: The Gurugram-based company, which went public in September 2025, is locked in a battle with Lightspeed-backed Snabbit and General Catalyst-backed Pronto in the high cash burn instant house help industry.

item.title: US, India must deepen cooperation on AI, semiconductors for shared security: Gina Raimondo
item.description: She recalled that during an earlier meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, their conversation centred on AI and the potential for India and the United States to collaborate in the field.

item.title: Blume, Kalaari, Chiratae among 19 VCs in RDI fund's Rs 7,131 crore first cohort
item.description: The selected cohort comprises 14 alternative investment funds (AIFs) and five focused research organisations (FROs), which will channel long-term capital into deeptech startups and private sector research and development.

item.title: Fortnite-maker Epic Games makes 'huge pivot' with AI, CEO says
item.description: Fortnite-maker Epic Games is making a "huge pivot" towards using artificial intelligence (AI) to boost video game development, CEO Tim Sweeney said on Monday. It also lands about six months after Epic said it would lay off more than 1,000 employees, though the company attributed the decision to broader issues like slower growth, rather than AI. Ramping up its use of AI internally now will increase Epic's ability "to survive the AI revolution, help other developers do the same, and come out on the other end making better code and content faster," Sweeney wrote on Monday.

item.title: Chips critical to India's future, but demand and management key to semiconductor push: N Chandrasekaran
item.description: India is well placed to strengthen its role in the global semiconductor industry due to its talent base and large domestic market, but businesses must carefully assess demand and manage investments as the sector expands, Tata Sons Chairman Natarajan Chandrasekaran said.

item.title: Fintech funding rises 14% to $2.2 billion in Jan-Sep; deal count falls 41%: Tracxn
item.description: Funding in the first nine months of 2025 stood at USD 1.9 billion. The number of rounds dropped to 153 from 260 a year ago, the data intelligence platform said in a report.

item.title: Character.AI files for bankruptcy, agrees to sell some assets to Disney for $20 million
item.description: Character.AI said on Monday it had filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in the US and agreed to sell some of its assets to Walt Disney for $20 million. The AI entertainment platform said it intends to continue operating as it completes the sale.

item.title: Nvidia's China AI-chip share falls as Huawei closes gap, report finds
item.description: Nvidia's share of China's market for data-centre AI chips fell to 34% in the first half of 2026, as US export controls restricted supplies of its products and domestic rivals led by Huawei gained ground, according to an IDC report seen by Reuters.

item.title: NTT Data in final talks to build Anthropic's first data centre in Japan, Nikkei reports
item.description: Japan's NTT Data Group, a unit of telecommunications giant NTT, is in the final stages of talks to build a data centre in Osaka, western Japan, for US AI company Anthropic, the Nikkei business daily reported on Tuesday, citing multiple sources.

item.title: Tencent sells dollar, dim sum bonds amid AI spending spree
item.description: Tencent Holdings is selling US dollar and offshore Chinese yuan, or dim sum, bonds in a deal that could raise at least $4.5 billion as the Chinese technology giant seeks funding amid higher spending on artificial intelligence.

item.title: Meta says its new AI models on par with OpenAI, Anthropic
item.description: Meta on Monday unveiled two new "frontier" artificial intelligence models called Wonder and Wonder Full, which the company claims perform at a level comparable to that of OpenAI's ChatGPT and Anthropic's Claude. In a blog post, Meta touted so-called benchmarking data from an independent firm called Artificial Analysis that appears to show that Meta's newest Wonder models outperform its own previous models, Spark, as well as various models developed by Anthropic, OpenAI and Google.

item.title: Anthropic says new safeguards sharply reduce AI distillation attacks
item.description: Anthropic said on Monday new measures designed to prevent rivals from copying the capabilities of its Claude AI models have reduced data harvested in so-called distillation attacks

item.title: Sarvam plans big fundraise; HCLTech's Q2 profit jumps
item.description: Happy Tuesday! Sarvam is in talks for a big round that could double its valuation to $3 billion. This and more in today’s ETtech Morning Dispatch.

item.title: Trump administration plans to move AI testing agency officials to White House: The Information
item.description: The Trump administration is planning to move three senior officials of the Center for Advancing Innovation and Standards for Super Intelligence to the White House, The Information reported on Monday, citing a White House official.

item.title: UK given access to safety-test latest AI models, minister says
item.description: Scrutiny of AI safety has intensified after developers including Anthropic and OpenAI disclosed instances of rogue or undesired behaviour by AI agents. Some industry figures have warned the technology could pose an existential threat to humanity.

item.title: Dating app Bumble in advanced talks to go private at $1 billion valuation, source says
item.description: Shares of Bumble rose around 21% in afternoon trading. Reuters exclusively reported earlier this year that Bumble is exploring a sale amid slowing growth in the online dating ​sector.
